ov: Small, shrimp-like marine crustaceans found in every ocean, near the bottom of the food chain. They eat phytoplankton and are the main food of many larger animals. Their swarms move up and down through the water each day, by up to 400 m.

why.et: Harvested as food for people and livestock since at least the 1800s.

rg: All oceans; the Antarctic krill in the Southern Ocean.
fx: The name comes from a Norwegian word meaning “small fry of fish”.
Antarctic krill shed their outer skeleton every 13 to 20 days.
